summary: 1959 41-foot Forest Service timber tower with R-6 cab in Pend Oreille County; staffed until 1981, restored by volunteers since 1995, reached by a gated road walk today.

facts.design: 41-foot treated timber tower with R-6 flattop live-in cab and catwalk

access.note: The access road gate is locked all year, so visitors walk in. The cab is locked. The catwalk was open on a 2018 visit, which is not a standing permission.

visit.trail_note: Walk of about 2.1 miles from the locked gate (Will Hite). TrailChick lists a 4.5-mile round trip with 1,100 feet of gain.

Pend Oreille Anthropological Society and the Forest Service began restoration as a Passport in Time project

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1959 is the present 41-foot tower. The first lookout, a 50-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab, dates to about 1932 per firelookout.com, Will Hite and TrailChick.

sources.title: Eastern Washington 2017 Chapter Report
sources.publisher: Forest Fire Lookout Association, Eastern Washington Chapter

notes_for_editor: Record location (48.52702, -117.452515) and the 1959 build year match NHLR, so no corrections. Elevation: the record's 1660.9 m matches NHLR's 5,449 ft; firelookout.com, Will Hite and TrailChick give 5,474 ft (about 1,669 m). Left out of facts. TrailChick's coordinates differ slightly from the record. The record's 2005 and 2009 restoration events, and the 2009 date for lightning protection and the rental program, could not be traced in the sources read. Will Hite dates the lightning protection and reroofing to summer 2007, so the 2009 entry needs checking against its source. Access 'restricted' is editorial: locked gate, locked cab, walk-in only. TrailChick's note that the catwalk was open in 2018 is not a standing permission, and the story does not encourage climbing. Rental status is unconfirmed: the 2017 chapter report gives plans, Will Hite gives 2007 preparation, and no current listing was found. The Colville 2017 report says two lookouts were in the rental program but does not name them. Will Hite gives five days of 2017 work; the chapter report gives a one-week session. Not contradictory, but noted. Photo licences (NHLR 2018 photo by Jarred Roberg; firelookout.com photo from the Fire Lookout Museum and Rex Kamstra) were not checked; no photos added.
